title: Generic fields and component orbits in a finite quotient of a normal scheme
statement: Let $X$ and $Z$ be normal Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains and Noetherian means a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings. Let a finite group $H$ act on $X$, and let $q:X\to Z$ be an invariant finite surjective morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] whose geometric fibres are $H$-orbits and whose structure sheaf satisfies $\mathcal O_Z=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^H$. Then $q$ maps generic points of $X$ to generic points of $Z$, and induces a bijection from $H$-orbits of irreducible components of $X$ to irreducible components of $Z$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point]. If $\eta$ is a generic point of $X$, $\xi=q(\eta)$, $M=\kappa(\eta)$ and $D=\{h\in H:h\eta=\eta\}$, the canonical residue-field embedding identifies $\kappa(\xi)$ with $M^D=\{a\in M:ha=a\text{ for every }h\in D\}$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The action of $D$ on $M$ need not be faithful. In particular, the assertion applies to disconnected $X$ without a generically free action.

source.place: Agent-formulated generic-localization consequence of Tag 03BK (lemma-invariants-base-change), part (3), for the finite constant action groupoid: localization to a generic point commutes with invariants, and invariants of a transitively permuted product of fields identify with the fixed field of a factor stabilizer. Used in ILO X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151, but no freeness or integral-source assumption is made here.
